summary: CASB urges the Commission not to narrow or sunset E-Rate without a record on what districts would lose, and to leave decisions on screen time, content, and internet safety policy content with elected local boards. CASB supports the program-integrity goals of the Further Notice but asks the Commission to refine several proposals. The comment opposes limiting or sunsetting E-Rate to save money and reduce program funding. The comment opposes narrowing the eligibility scope for E-Rate, arguing that eligibility based on district size alone is inadequate and that documentation and comparison requirements can address cost-effectiveness more precisely.

claims.argument: Eligibility based on district size alone would be a poor fit
claims.evidence_quote: Eligibility based on district size alone would be a poor fit, and documentation and comparison requirements would address cost-effectiveness more precisely.
